extraction.name: MVBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive multi-modal video understanding benchmark covering 20 challenging temporal video tasks, built by converting public video annotations into multiple-choice QA for evaluating MLLMs' temporal understanding.
extraction.creator: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Videos were selected from 11 public video datasets and automatically converted into multiple-choice QA pairs guided by temporal task definitions. The collection process included filtering for diversity, temporal sensitivity, and question difficulty.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Public videos and annotations from 11 datasets: STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The benchmark converts selected video annotations into multiple-choice QA format using ChatGPT and template-based option construction, then samples and shuffles answer options and normalizes option lengths with an LLM.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos were filtered to ensure diversity, temporal sensitivity, and balanced difficulty. Short clips with negligible motion and extremely long videos with overly complicated contexts were removed; selected videos were primarily 5s to 35s long. Additional dataset-specific filtering criteria were applied.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were automatically generated as multiple-choice QA pairs from public video annotations. ChatGPT was used to generate questions for tasks requiring QA generation, while answer options were created either from templates based on ground-truth annotations or by ChatGPT for some tasks such as Unexpected Action.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors used multiple-choice QA instead of open-ended answers to improve evaluation correctness and fairness, avoiding biased scoring by LLMs or manual intervention. They also processed answer options to avoid answer leakage by equalizing option lengths.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: First-person and third-person perspectives; indoor and outdoor environments; characters and persons appearing in videos.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to support fairer and more accurate evaluation of temporal understanding in MLLMs and to advance general video understanding.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark is designed to avoid biased scoring from LLM-based evaluation, but there is a minimal source gap between instruction data and MVBench because CLEVRER and SthSthV2-related data overlap with some benchmark tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Some tasks remain difficult for current MLLMs, especially position, count, character, egocentric navigation, and episodic reasoning. Visual information alone may be insufficient for some cognition tasks, and related tuning data may be lacking.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation benchmark for testing temporal understanding capabilities of multi-modal large language models on 20 video understanding tasks.
